stem: Out of the following which is a Pythagorean triplet?
solution: A Pythagorean triplet satisfies \(a^2 + b^2 = c^2\). For \((3, 4, 5)\): \(3^2 + 4^2 = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5^2\). Hence \((3, 4, 5)\) is a Pythagorean triplet.

stem: \(\angle ACB\) is an inscribed angle in a circle with centre O. If \(\angle ACB = 65^\circ\), then what is the measure of its intercepted arc AXB?
solution: The measure of an inscribed angle is half the measure of its intercepted arc. \(\therefore m(\text{arc AXB}) = 2 \times \angle ACB = 2 \times 65^\circ = 130^\circ\).

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: If the radius of a cone is 5 cm and its perpendicular height is 12 cm, then the slant height is ________.
solution: Slant height \(l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2} = \sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13\) cm.

subtopic: Ratio of Areas of Two Triangles
stem: In the following figure \(\triangle ABC\), \(B\text{–}D\text{–}C\) and \(BD = 7\), \(BC = 20\), then find \(\dfrac{A(\triangle ABD)}{A(\triangle ABC)}\).
solution: \(\triangle ABD\) and \(\triangle ABC\) have the same height (the perpendicular from vertex A to line BC). Triangles with equal heights have areas proportional to their bases. \(\therefore \dfrac{A(\triangle ABD)}{A(\triangle ABC)} = \dfrac{BD}{BC} = \dfrac{7}{20}\).
figureNote: triangle ABC with D on side BC (B-D-C); cevian AD drawn, p-02

stem: In the following figure \(\angle MNP = 90^\circ\), seg \(NQ \perp\) seg \(MP\), \(MQ = 9\), \(QP = 4\), find \(NQ\).
solution: In a right-angled triangle, the perpendicular drawn from the right-angle vertex to the hypotenuse is the geometric mean of the two segments of the hypotenuse. \(\therefore NQ^2 = MQ \times QP = 9 \times 4 = 36 \Rightarrow NQ = 6\).
figureNote: right-angled triangle MNP, right angle at N; NQ perpendicular to hypotenuse MP with Q on MP, p-02

stem: The angle made by a line with the positive direction of the X-axis is \(30^\circ\). Find the slope of that line.
solution: Slope \(= \tan\theta = \tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).

stem: In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, \(m\angle A = 100^\circ\), then find \(m\angle C\).
solution: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary. \(\therefore m\angle A + m\angle C = 180^\circ \Rightarrow m\angle C = 180^\circ - 100^\circ = 80^\circ\).

subtopic: Area of Sector and Segment of a Circle
stem: The radius of a circle with centre P is 10 cm. If chord AB of the circle subtends a right angle at P, find the area of the minor sector P-AXB by completing the activity. (\(\pi = 3.14\))
solution: \(r = 10\) cm, \(\theta = 90^\circ\), \(\pi = 3.14\). \(A(P\text{-}AXB) = \dfrac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^2 = \dfrac{90}{360} \times 3.14 \times 10^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 314 = 78.5\) sq. cm.
figureNote: circle with centre P and radius 10; chord AB subtends a right angle at P (right-angle mark at P); minor arc AXB with point X on the circle below AB, p-03

stem: In the following figure, chord MN and chord RS intersect at point D. If \(RD = 15\), \(DS = 4\), \(MD = 8\), find \(DN\) by completing the activity.
solution: By the theorem of internal division of chords, \(MD \times DN = RD \times DS\). \(\therefore 8 \times DN = 15 \times 4 = 60 \Rightarrow DN = \dfrac{60}{8} = 7.5\).
figureNote: circle with chords MN and RS intersecting internally at point D; M and R on the left, S and N on the right, p-04

stem: An observer at a distance of 10 m from a tree looks at the top of the tree; the angle of elevation is \(60^\circ\). Find the height of the tree by completing the activity. (\(\sqrt{3} = 1.73\))
solution: In right-angled \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle ABC = 90^\circ\), \(AB = h\) = height of the tree, \(BC = 10\) m = distance of the observer from the tree, and the angle of elevation \(\theta = \angle BCA = 60^\circ\). \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{AB}{BC}\), so \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{AB}{BC} \Rightarrow \dfrac{AB}{BC} = \sqrt{3}\). \(\therefore AB = BC \times \sqrt{3} = 10\sqrt{3} = 10 \times 1.73 = 17.3\) m. Height of the tree \(= 17.3\) m.
figureNote: right-angled triangle ABC, right angle at B; observer at C, tree AB vertical; angle of elevation 60 degrees at C, BC = 10 m, p-05

stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(DE \parallel BC\). If \(DB = 5.4\) cm, \(AD = 1.8\) cm, \(EC = 7.2\) cm, then find \(AE\).
solution: By the Basic Proportionality Theorem, \(\dfrac{AD}{DB} = \dfrac{AE}{EC}\). \(\therefore \dfrac{1.8}{5.4} = \dfrac{AE}{7.2} \Rightarrow AE = \dfrac{1.8 \times 7.2}{5.4} = \dfrac{12.96}{5.4} = 2.4\) cm.
figureNote: triangle ABC with D on AB and E on AC, segment DE parallel to BC, p-06

stem: In the figure given below, find \(RS\) and \(PS\) using the information given in \(\triangle PSR\).
solution: In \(\triangle PSR\), \(\angle S = 90^\circ\), \(\angle P = 30^\circ\) and hypotenuse \(PR = 12\). \(RS = PR \sin 30^\circ = 12 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 6\). \(PS = PR \cos 30^\circ = 12 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 6\sqrt{3}\).
figureNote: right-angled triangle PSR, right angle at S; hypotenuse RP = 12, angle at P = 30 degrees, p-06

subtopic: Tangent and Secant to a Circle
stem: In the following figure, a circle with centre D touches the sides of \(\angle ACB\) at A and B. If \(\angle ACB = 52^\circ\), find the measure of \(\angle ADB\).
solution: CA and CB are tangents to the circle, so the radii DA and DB are perpendicular to them: \(\angle DAC = \angle DBC = 90^\circ\). In quadrilateral DACB, the sum of all angles is \(360^\circ\). \(\therefore \angle ADB + \angle DAC + \angle ACB + \angle DBC = 360^\circ \Rightarrow \angle ADB + 90^\circ + 52^\circ + 90^\circ = 360^\circ \Rightarrow \angle ADB = 128^\circ\).
figureNote: angle ACB with vertex C; a circle with centre D inscribed touching the two arms (tangent at A on the upper arm and B on the lower arm), p-07

stem: Verify whether the points \(A(1, -3)\), \(B(2, -5)\) and \(C(-4, 7)\) are collinear or not.
If \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{11}{61}\), find the value of \(\cos\theta\) using a trigonometric identity.
solution: \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1 \Rightarrow \cos^2\theta = 1 - \left(\dfrac{11}{61}\right)^2 = 1 - \dfrac{121}{3721} = \dfrac{3600}{3721}\). \(\therefore \cos\theta = \dfrac{60}{61}\).

stem: In the following figure, \(XY \parallel\) seg AC. If \(2AX = 3BX\) and \(XY = 9\), complete the activity to find the value of AC.
solution: \(2AX = 3BX \Rightarrow \dfrac{AX}{BX} = \dfrac{3}{2}\). By componendo, \(\dfrac{AX + BX}{BX} = \dfrac{3 + 2}{2} \Rightarrow \dfrac{AB}{BX} = \dfrac{5}{2}\) ...(I). In \(\triangle BCA\) and \(\triangle BYX\): \(\angle BCA \cong \angle BYX\) (corresponding angles, \(XY \parallel AC\)) and \(\angle B\) is common, so \(\triangle BCA \sim \triangle BYX\) (AA test of similarity). \(\therefore \dfrac{BA}{BX} = \dfrac{AC}{XY}\) (corresponding sides of similar triangles). From (I), \(\dfrac{5}{2} = \dfrac{AC}{9} \Rightarrow AC = \dfrac{5 \times 9}{2} = 22.5\).
figureNote: triangle ABC with A at top, B lower-left, C lower-right; X on AB and Y on BC, segment XY parallel to AC, p-07

stem: Complete the activity to prove that the sum of the squares of the diagonals of a rhombus is equal to the sum of the squares of its sides. (\(\square PQRS\) is a rhombus; diagonals PR and SQ intersect each other at point T.)
solution: Given: \(\square PQRS\) is a rhombus; diagonals PR and SQ intersect at T. To prove: \(PS^2 + SR^2 + QR^2 + PQ^2 = PR^2 + QS^2\). Diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other, so T is the midpoint of both PR and SQ. In \(\triangle PQS\), PT is the median and in \(\triangle QRS\), RT is the median. By Apollonius theorem: \(PQ^2 + PS^2 = 2PT^2 + 2QT^2\) ...(I) and \(QR^2 + SR^2 = 2RT^2 + 2QT^2\) ...(II). Adding (I) and (II): \(PQ^2 + PS^2 + QR^2 + SR^2 = 2(PT^2 + RT^2) + 4QT^2\). Since \(RT = PT\), \(= 2(PT^2 + PT^2) + 4QT^2 = 4PT^2 + 4QT^2 = (2PT)^2 + (2QT)^2 = PR^2 + QS^2\). \(\therefore PS^2 + SR^2 + QR^2 + PQ^2 = PR^2 + QS^2\).
figureNote: rhombus PQRS with both diagonals PR and SQ drawn, intersecting at T; equal-length tick marks on all four sides, p-08

stem: Show that the points \(P(1, -2)\), \(Q(5, 2)\), \(R(3, -1)\), \(S(-1, -5)\) are the vertices of a parallelogram.
solution: For \(\square PQRS\) to be a parallelogram, its diagonals PR and QS must bisect each other. Midpoint of PR \(= \left(\dfrac{1+3}{2}, \dfrac{-2+(-1)}{2}\right) = \left(2, -\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\). Midpoint of QS \(= \left(\dfrac{5+(-1)}{2}, \dfrac{2+(-5)}{2}\right) = \left(2, -\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\). The midpoints coincide, so the diagonals bisect each other. \(\therefore\) PQRS is a parallelogram.

stem: Prove that the tangent segments drawn from an external point to a circle are congruent.
solution: Given: A circle with centre O; P is a point in the exterior; PA and PB are tangent segments touching the circle at A and B. To prove: \(PA \cong PB\). Construction: Draw seg OA, seg OB and seg OP. Proof: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so \(\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^\circ\). In right-angled \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\): \(OA = OB\) (radii of the same circle) and hypotenuse \(OP = OP\) (common side). \(\therefore \triangle OAP \cong \triangle OBP\) (hypotenuse-side test). \(\therefore PA = PB\) (corresponding sides of congruent triangles), i.e. the tangent segments are congruent.

subtopic: Construction of a Tangent to a Circle
stem: Draw a circle with radius 4.1 cm. Construct tangents to the circle from a point at a distance of 7.3 cm from the centre.
solution: Steps of construction: (1) Draw a circle with centre O and radius 4.1 cm. (2) Take a point P such that \(OP = 7.3\) cm and draw seg OP. (3) Draw the perpendicular bisector of seg OP; let it meet OP at M. (4) With M as centre and radius MO \((= MP)\), draw an arc cutting the circle at points A and B. (5) Draw lines PA and PB. Then PA and PB are the required tangents from P. (Since P, A, O, B lie on a circle with diameter OP, \(\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^\circ\), so PA and PB touch the circle at A and B.)

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: How many solid cylinders of radius 10 cm and height 6 cm can be made by melting a solid sphere of radius 30 cm?
solution: Volume of the sphere \(= \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi (30)^3 = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi \times 27000 = 36000\pi\) cm\(^3\). Volume of one cylinder \(= \pi R^2 h = \pi (10)^2 \times 6 = 600\pi\) cm\(^3\). Number of cylinders \(= \dfrac{36000\pi}{600\pi} = 60\).

subtopic: Theorem of Areas of Similar Triangles
context: In the following figure \(DE \parallel BC\), then:
stem: If \(DE = 4\) cm, \(BC = 8\) cm, \(A(\triangle ADE) = 25\) cm\(^2\), find \(A(\triangle ABC)\).
solution: Since \(DE \parallel BC\), \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\). By the theorem of areas of similar triangles, \(\dfrac{A(\triangle ADE)}{A(\triangle ABC)} = \dfrac{DE^2}{BC^2} = \dfrac{4^2}{8^2} = \dfrac{1}{4}\). \(\therefore A(\triangle ABC) = 4 \times A(\triangle ADE) = 4 \times 25 = 100\) cm\(^2\).
figureNote: triangle ABC with B at top, A lower-left, C lower-right; D on AB and E on AC, segment DE parallel to BC, p-10

subtopic: Theorem of Areas of Similar Triangles
context: In the following figure \(DE \parallel BC\), then:
stem: If \(DE : BC = 3 : 5\), then find \(A(\triangle ADE) : A(\square DBCE)\).
solution: Since \(DE \parallel BC\), \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\). \(\dfrac{A(\triangle ADE)}{A(\triangle ABC)} = \dfrac{DE^2}{BC^2} = \dfrac{3^2}{5^2} = \dfrac{9}{25}\). Let \(A(\triangle ADE) = 9k\); then \(A(\triangle ABC) = 25k\). \(A(\square DBCE) = A(\triangle ABC) - A(\triangle ADE) = 25k - 9k = 16k\). \(\therefore A(\triangle ADE) : A(\square DBCE) = 9k : 16k = 9 : 16\).
figureNote: triangle ABC with B at top, A lower-left, C lower-right; D on AB and E on AC, segment DE parallel to BC (same figure as Q4(1)(i)), p-10

stem: \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQR\). In \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB = 3.6\) cm, \(BC = 4\) cm and \(AC = 4.2\) cm. The corresponding sides of \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle PQR\) are in the ratio \(2 : 3\). Construct \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle PQR\).
solution: Since \(\dfrac{\text{side of } \triangle ABC}{\text{side of } \triangle PQR} = \dfrac{2}{3}\), \(\triangle PQR\) is the larger triangle with sides \(PQ = \dfrac{3}{2}(3.6) = 5.4\) cm, \(QR = \dfrac{3}{2}(4) = 6\) cm, \(PR = \dfrac{3}{2}(4.2) = 6.3\) cm. Steps of construction: (1) Construct \(\triangle ABC\) with \(AB = 3.6\) cm, \(BC = 4\) cm, \(AC = 4.2\) cm. (2) Draw ray BX making an acute angle with BC on the side opposite to A. (3) On ray BX mark 3 points \(B_1, B_2, B_3\) such that \(BB_1 = B_1B_2 = B_2B_3\). (4) Join \(B_2C\); through \(B_3\) draw a line parallel to \(B_2C\) meeting ray BC (produced) at R, so that \(BR = \dfrac{3}{2}BC = 6\) cm. (5) Through R draw a line parallel to CA meeting ray BA (produced) at P. Then \(\triangle PBR\) (taking \(Q = B\)) is the required \(\triangle PQR\) similar to \(\triangle ABC\) with ratio \(2 : 3\).

context: The radii of the circular ends of a frustum of a cone are 14 cm and 8 cm. The height of the frustum is 8 cm. (\(\pi = 3.14\))
stem: Find the curved surface area of the frustum.
solution: Let \(R = 14\) cm, \(r = 8\) cm, \(h = 8\) cm. Slant height \(l = \sqrt{h^2 + (R - r)^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + (14 - 8)^2} = \sqrt{64 + 36} = \sqrt{100} = 10\) cm. Curved surface area \(= \pi (R + r) l = 3.14 \times (14 + 8) \times 10 = 3.14 \times 22 \times 10 = 690.8\) cm\(^2\).

context: The radii of the circular ends of a frustum of a cone are 14 cm and 8 cm. The height of the frustum is 8 cm. (\(\pi = 3.14\))
stem: Find the total surface area of the frustum.
solution: With \(R = 14\) cm, \(r = 8\) cm and slant height \(l = 10\) cm, total surface area \(= \pi(R + r)l + \pi R^2 + \pi r^2 = 690.8 + 3.14 \times 14^2 + 3.14 \times 8^2 = 690.8 + 615.44 + 200.96 = 1507.2\) cm\(^2\).

context: The radii of the circular ends of a frustum of a cone are 14 cm and 8 cm. The height of the frustum is 8 cm. (\(\pi = 3.14\))
stem: Find the volume of the frustum.
solution: Volume \(= \dfrac{1}{3}\pi h (R^2 + r^2 + Rr) = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 3.14 \times 8 \times (14^2 + 8^2 + 14 \times 8) = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 3.14 \times 8 \times (196 + 64 + 112) = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 3.14 \times 8 \times 372 = 3114.88\) cm\(^3\).

stem: \(\square ABCD\) is a rectangle. Taking AD as a diameter, a semicircle AXD is drawn which intersects the diagonal BD at X. If \(AB = 12\) cm, \(AD = 9\) cm, then find the values of BD and BX.
solution: In rectangle ABCD, \(\angle DAB = 90^\circ\), so in right-angled \(\triangle DAB\): \(BD = \sqrt{AB^2 + AD^2} = \sqrt{12^2 + 9^2} = \sqrt{144 + 81} = \sqrt{225} = 15\) cm. AD is the diameter of the semicircle and X lies on it, so \(\angle AXD = 90^\circ\) (angle in a semicircle); hence \(AX \perp BD\), i.e. AX is the altitude from the right-angle vertex A onto the hypotenuse BD of \(\triangle DAB\). By the property of similar right-angled triangles, \(AB^2 = BX \times BD\). \(\therefore 12^2 = BX \times 15 \Rightarrow BX = \dfrac{144}{15} = 9.6\) cm.

context: Taking \(\theta = 30^\circ\), verify the following trigonometric identities:
stem: \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\)
solution: At \(\theta = 30^\circ\): \(\sin 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}\), \(\cos 30^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). LHS \(= \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4} = 1 = \) RHS. Verified.

context: Taking \(\theta = 30^\circ\), verify the following trigonometric identities:
stem: \(1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta\)
solution: At \(\theta = 30^\circ\): \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), \(\sec 30^\circ = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\). LHS \(= 1 + \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2 = 1 + \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\). RHS \(= \left(\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2 = \dfrac{4}{3}\). LHS = RHS. Verified.

context: Taking \(\theta = 30^\circ\), verify the following trigonometric identities:
stem: \(1 + \cot^2\theta = \operatorname{cosec}^2\theta\)
solution: At \(\theta = 30^\circ\): \(\cot 30^\circ = \sqrt{3}\), \(\operatorname{cosec} 30^\circ = 2\). LHS \(= 1 + (\sqrt{3})^2 = 1 + 3 = 4\). RHS \(= 2^2 = 4\). LHS = RHS. Verified.
